Someone has chalked a small ear on the railing.|You know the dome's geography now: by the pillar you hear the front desk; by the window, the stacks.} {Two voices below are discussing a test that hasn't been set yet.|Someone below is rehearsing a proposal of marriage, badly.|{season == "winter": The radiators hiss over half of it.|A prefect is reading out demerits to himself, with relish.}} Lean on the rail and listen {You learn the third question of next week's test, probably. Eavesdroppers, it turns out, don't feel as clever as they'd hoped.|The proposal ends in a yes, and you weren't invited. You feel like a thief who has stolen a wedding.|You learn exactly what the front desk thinks of you. It's fair, which is worse.} Cough loudly, and read {Your cough rolls down the dome like thunder. Seven floors stop whispering at once, and you read in a silence you made.|You cough. Somewhere below, the proposal stops mid-sentence. You read a whole chapter before you stop wondering how it ended.|You cough on purpose now. Below, every whisper stops, and the dome is yours, and so is the chapter.}
